policy: Each entry is a temporary file-level exception to the 90% lines/functions and 85% branches gate. Global coverage remains enforced by Vitest. Exceptions are evidence of an explicit gap, not an exclusion from product coverage.

entries.reason: Framework error boundary branches require a rendered Next runtime failure to exercise.
Account failure and reconciliation branches require browser fault injection.
Administrative session and dead-letter recovery branches require authenticated browser actions and explicit confirmation flows.
Dashboard degraded and realtime branches require browser/runtime failure scenarios.
Indicator fallback branches are validated by the responsive browser lane, not isolated component fixtures.
Notification recovery and empty-state branches require browser interaction coverage.
Patient workspace degraded branches require browser fault injection and scoped runtime fixtures.
Request-detail failure branches are coupled to route navigation and server responses.
Result attachment and reconciliation branches require the clinical browser lifecycle.
Queue pagination and realtime recovery branches require browser interaction coverage.
Defensive operational-context fallbacks are policy-dependent and require scenario fixtures.
Registry conflict and context branches require broader clinical fixture combinations.
Pure model normalization and legacy envelope branches are exercised through persistence suites.
Corrupt-manifest and filesystem failure branches require destructive recovery drills.
External scanner transport and policy branches require a scanner test service.
Migration rollback and malformed metadata branches require disposable PostgreSQL execution.
Database constraint and projection failure branches require PostgreSQL integration.
Relational cutover branches require a live schema and multi-row PostgreSQL fixtures.
Backfill interruption and reconciliation branches require a disposable relational dataset.
Relational read degradation branches require a live normalized schema.
Cutover mismatch and rollback branches require a live relational integration scenario.
Production PostgreSQL and runtime shutdown branches require environment-isolated integration tests.
